content.title: China's Anta Sports exploring bid for Puma, Bloomberg reports
content.summary:
STORY: Chinese sportswear maker Anta is reportedly one of the firms exploring a potential takeover of the German sportswear brand Puma.

The report from Bloomberg News on Thursday said Anta has been working with an adviser to evaluate a bid, and may team up with a private equity firm if it decides to move forward with an offer.

The report cited people familiar with the matter.

Anta Sports declined to comment on the report when contacted by Reuters.

Shares in Puma rose around 13% in early deals.

Other potential bidders could include Chinese sportswear group Li Ning.

And Puma could also attract interest from Japanese sportswear company ASICS.

Puma's biggest shareholder Artemis, the privately-owned holding company that controls Gucci owner Kering, said it is considering all options for its 29% stake in the sportswear brand.

Puma recently announced it was cutting 900 corporate jobs as part of a turnaround plan.

That's after lower demand for its products and a hit from U.S. tariffs on imports impacted its business.

Puma's market valuation is currently $2.92 billion, according to LSEG data.

Its share price has halved since the start of this year, as it is losing ground to rivals in an increasingly competitive sportswear market.
